claims: Gary Woodland won the 2019 U.S. Open at Pebble Beach.
Gary Woodland won the Texas Children’s Houston Open in March 2026.
The Texas Children’s Houston Open was Gary Woodland's first victory since the 2019 U.S. Open.
Gary Woodland finished 21 under at Memorial Park in the Texas Children’s Houston Open.
Gary Woodland won the Texas Children’s Houston Open by five shots.
Gary Woodland broke down in tears after his final putt in the Texas Children’s Houston Open.
Gary Woodland embraced his wife and team after winning the Texas Children’s Houston Open.
In August 2023, Gary Woodland announced he had a lesion on his brain.
Gary Woodland underwent surgery in September 2023 to remove the tumor.
Gary Woodland's surgery to remove the tumor was successful.
Gary Woodland's tumor was pressing on the part of his brain that controls fear and anxiety.
Gary Woodland's tumor created significant unprovoked anxiety symptoms.
Before the surgery, Gary Woodland wrote letters to his wife and children fearing he might not survive.
Gary Woodland returned to the PGA Tour in January 2024.
Gary Woodland admitted to dealing with intense hidden anxiety and post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD).
Gary Woodland stated he felt like he was "dying inside" while trying to live a normal life on tour.
Gary Woodland suffered from intense hypervigilance where strangers approaching from behind would trigger panic.
Gary Woodland suffered from blurred vision during competition at times.
In 2024, Gary Woodland missed 11 of 26 cuts.
Gary Woodland finished 155th in the 2024 FedExCup.
